workload.description: One entry of the main input a helper reads, writes or judges: an exception record, a finding, a rule of a policy config, a requirement field or a classification. Each function says which. 640 is a very large registry.

contribution.description: Called once per run, between reading and writing the registry, but not attributed: the end-to-end run reconciles a registry in which every finding matches, while this benchmark holds the registry at 640 records with only some findings matching, so its time would misstate that share.
Once per run, after reconciling, when the registry changed.

reconcileExceptions.input.deriveId: fixed: reads one field of the finding, the cheapest honest derivation
reconcileExceptions.input.createStub: fixed: returns the finding as the record, the cheapest honest stub, so the benchmark measures the reconciliation and not a caller's stub builder

loadExceptionRegistry.input.path: fixed: a short relative path, because a path's length does not change the work
loadExceptionRegistry.input.schema: fixed: a schema that accepts every array, so the benchmark measures the reader and not a validator
loadExceptionRegistry.input.readFile: fixed: an in-memory stand-in, as the standard asks (no real I/O)

writeExceptionRegistry.input.path: fixed: a short relative path, because a path's length does not change the work
writeExceptionRegistry.input.readFile: fixed: an in-memory stand-in that returns the old text, so every run rewrites
writeExceptionRegistry.input.writeFile: fixed: an in-memory stand-in, as the standard asks (no real I/O)
writeExceptionRegistry.input.rename: fixed: an in-memory stand-in, as the standard asks (no real I/O)
writeExceptionRegistry.input.isSymlink: fixed: an in-memory stand-in that says the path is a regular file

resolveExceptionPolicy.classification.group: fixed: one group, because a config's groups are looked up by name
resolveExceptionPolicy.globalDefault.requirements: not covered: only an `exception` default carries requirements, and the benchmark's default is `forbidden`

evaluateExceptionRecord.input.fieldValue: fixed: reads one field of the record
evaluateExceptionRecord.input.globalDefault: fixed: `forbidden`, which only applies to a group the config does not name, and the benchmark's group is named
evaluateExceptionRecord.input.record: fixed: one record with every field filled, so every requirement is checked

hashRequirementFields.record: fixed: one record with every field filled
hashRequirementFields.fieldValue: fixed: reads one field of the record
